entries.mechanism: TAXSIM runs at its latest 2024 law year and reports 19945.51 for the married 300,000-dollar filer; the 2026 pipeline reports 16752.80. The 2026 value uses the lower Chapter-59-of-2025 rate schedule plus the 2026 section 601(d) supplemental recapture, while the 2024 TAXSIM value applies the higher pre-2026 rates and the 2024 tax-table-benefit recapture, which flat-rates a larger share of income at this level. The 3,192.71-dollar gap is the 2024-to-2026 rate-cut and recapture vintage, not a pipeline defect: the 2026 main bracket tax alone (15612.80) is close to the 2024 main bracket tax (about 16670 on the same 283,950 taxable base), so most of the gap is the differing 2024 supplemental recapture.

For the married 60,000-dollar filer the 2026 pipeline reports 2040.80 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 2084.75, a 43.95-dollar gap. There is no supplemental recapture at this income, so the residual is purely the 2024-versus-2026 marginal-rate difference on the 43,950-dollar taxable base from the Chapter 59 of the Laws of 2025 rate reductions.

For the single 30,000-dollar filer the 2026 pipeline reports 1023.00 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 1045.00, a 22.00-dollar gap. There is no supplemental recapture at this income, so the residual is purely the 2024-versus-2026 marginal-rate difference on the 22,000-dollar taxable base from the Chapter 59 of the Laws of 2025 rate reductions.

For the single 150,000-dollar filer the 2026 pipeline reports 8289.9990 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 8723.09, a 433.09-dollar gap. Both include a supplemental recapture, so the residual combines the 2024-versus-2026 bracket-rate reduction and the differing 2024 recapture magnitude, a documented law vintage.
